ledger.claim: The driver never arrived at the pickup point. EV-GPS-00625 carries 55 driver fixes, and its derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0 — across the entire trace the driver is never once inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, his closest approach being min_distance_m 377.4 m (the 50 m radius and the 25 m accuracy filter both come from fee_schedule and are tagged to POLICY-NO-SHOW). Because no qualifying in-radius fix exists anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 18:09:40 cancellation, POL-NS-02 deems the driver not to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the S$4.00 cancellation fee.

The 18:04:00 'arrived' event is a false marker, and it is caught by both of POL-NS-05's independent triggers. At that timestamp the driver is more than 300 m from the pin — his minimum distance for the whole trace is 377.4 m, so he is never within 300 m — and his recorded speed at that time sits in the 40.6 to 43.5 km/h band, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold. The false marker does not start the waiting clock, and because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05 limb (ii) requires the fee refunded in full, no driver compensation payable, and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. The trip record's wait_time_min of 5.7 is measured from that false marker and cannot cure the defect.

Even taken at its highest the waiting period is zero. The effective in-geofence dwell computed under POL-NS-02 is longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0, against the 300-second minimum for the STANDARD zone class, a shortfall of 300 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full — expressly whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider answered messages. This is the cleanest arithmetic route to the rider's full refund: state the 300-second minimum, state the 0-second measured dwell, state the 300-second shortfall.

The driver cannot rescue the dwell by accumulating separate intervals. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits accumulation only where a traffic advisory that is present and populated, of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, covers the pickup road and the waiting period. EV-ADVIS-00625-01 is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the pickup road in this window'), weight_multiplier 0.0 — so limb (i) is unavailable to the driver and its four admissible advisory types are absent. In any event the trace returns run_count 0 and no second in-geofence interval: there is nothing to sum. I cite the missing artifact for its absence only, as the rules permit; a MISSING artifact can carry no fact and I do not ask it to.

POL-NS-01 limbs (c) and (d) fail as well, and they fail on the drafting choice the clause itself insists on. Limb (c) measures the continuous dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, NOT from the driver's 'arrived' tap; there is no qualifying in-geofence fix at all, so no continuous 300-second hold was ever completed. Limb (d) then requires the trip to have been terminated by the driver with a qualifying reason code at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed — and no required dwell ever elapsed. Independently, the record shows the cancellation was made by the SYSTEM (cancelled_by 'SYSTEM', status CANCELLED_BY_SYSTEM), with started_at and ended_at both null, so there is no driver-initiated termination of the trip to found the limb on either.

Assume for the driver the most favourable reading available to him — that he was somewhere near the pin rather than at it. It does not help him. POL-NS-03 is a rider-exonerating route, not a driver one: on its own terms the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. And its predicate is not met here in any case. POL-NS-03 applies only where the trace shows the driver stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin; the driver's trace shows him in continuous motion at 40 to 59 km/h with a minimum distance of 377.4 m and a qualifying in-geofence hold of zero seconds, so there is no stationary hold anywhere in the trip and POL-NS-03 has nothing to attach to.

The chat corroborates the rider's account and removes any basis to read the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code as a genuine no-show under POL-NS-01. At 18:06:40 the driver wrote 'ERP 25 each cash', an off-platform cash demand for both occupants; the rider replied at 18:07:20 'what? no. I'm getting out at the petrol station'. The priced ledger records tolls_erp 0.00 and an optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00, so the cash demand has no basis in this trip, and the driver's own account concedes he combined two bookings into one vehicle. This is the record of a journey already under way with passengers aboard and a driver monetising it off-app — not a rider who failed to turn up at the kerb — and it is the reason the reason code cannot bear the weight limb (d) would put on it.

This case is decidable on its merits and none of the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers fires, so the Judge should rule rather than hold the fee. Every artifact in the bundle carries admissibility status COMPLETE and weight_multiplier 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence and neither POL-NS-09(a) (confidence floor) nor POL-NS-09(e) (sole impaired evidence) is engaged; under POL-GEN-02 the confidence cap is therefore 1.0. The only sub-1.0 artifact is the absent advisory at weight 0.0, and nothing decides this case on it. The profile counters that POL-NS-09(c) and (d) read are all zero — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d 0, rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0, driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 — so no abuse trigger fires either. Every threshold fact (50 m radius, 300-second minimum, 25 m accuracy filter) is drawn from fee_schedule and applied to a clean 55-fix, gap-free trace. There is nothing here for a human reviewer to settle; the rider's claim should be upheld in full.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on this record: the trip carries no boarding event at any point - started_at and ended_at are both null and the trip terminated as CANCELLED_BY_SYSTEM under the recognised reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW - and the rider's own account ('He never pressed picked up') confirms that no boarding was ever registered in the app, so the termination limb of the anchor clause is not in issue.

The rider is not exonerated by POL-NS-04. Limb (a) fails because her only chat message ('what? no. I'm getting out at the petrol station') refuses an off-platform cash demand rather than locating her position, naming an entrance, block or bay, requesting the driver's position, or saying she cannot see the vehicle. Limb (c) also fails on her own track: her six fixes average 320.7 m from the pickup pin (min 319.2 m, max 321.8 m), more than three times the 100 m rider presence radius for a STANDARD zone, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0.

The rider's account that she was sitting in the driver's back seat is contradicted by her own device: across 18:03:40 to 18:04:25 all six of her fixes report 0.0 kph, while the driver's track over the same minutes reports continuous motion at 40.6 to 59.1 kph. A handset travelling in that vehicle could not have been stationary at 320 m from the pin throughout, so her narrative of being carried in the car is not supported by the trace she brings.

The amount charged is not defective. The cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 is exactly the figure produced by fee_schedule.resolution_rule - the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) - so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) that could be used to disturb the amount independently of the arrival question.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on this driver. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110, a ratio of about 0.009, so neither the absolute limb (4 or more terminations) nor the rate limb (above 0.08) is met, and nothing in POL-NS-07 withholds the driver's 80 percent share - SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00 fee - on this record. These are the only two profile counters the clause reads.

The present state of the ledger is a charge of SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so on this rider-filed dispute the contested amount is not returned unless the rider's own case displaces the charge; the default is not a refund.

The trip record and the driver's own trace contradict each other directly on arrival and dwell: the record asserts an arrival event at 18:04:00 followed by a 5.7 minute wait, while the trace places the driver never closer than 377.4 m from the pin, with zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and zero accumulated dwell at any point. Two admissible artifacts conflict head-on on the very facts that decide this fee, and on this record that conflict is not resolved for the driver by any clause in the category; POL-NS-09(b) directs such a case to a human reviewer, where the disputed fee is held rather than refunded by the automated pipeline.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling goes to both parties. The SGD 4.00 no-show fee charged on trip TRP-00625 is refunded in full to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable.

WHY THE FEE DOES NOT STAND. The charge is chargeable only if POL-NS-01 holds in every limb. Limb (b) requires the GPS trace to place the driver inside the STANDARD 50 m pickup geofence at or before the 'arrived' event. The trace (EV-GPS-00625, 55 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0) never brings the driver closer than 377.4 m to the pin and returns qualifying_fix_count 0, so limb (b) fails. Limb (c) requires a continuous 300-second in-geofence hold measured from the first qualifying fix: the measured qualifying hold is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, so limb (c) fails. Limb (d) requires the driver to have terminated the trip under a recognised reason code at or after that dwell elapsed; no dwell ever elapsed, and the termination was made by the platform (cancelled_by 'SYSTEM', status CANCELLED_BY_SYSTEM) with started_at and ended_at null, so limb (d) cannot carry the fee either.

The 18:04:00 'arrived' marker is a false marker under POL-NS-05, caught by both of its independent triggers: at that timestamp the driver was 377.4 m from the pin (more than 300 m) and moving at 40.6 to 43.5 km/h (above the 15 km/h motion threshold). The waiting clock therefore recomputes to run from a first qualifying in-geofence fix that does not exist anywhere in the trip, and POL-NS-05(ii) requires the fee refunded in full with no compensation payable and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event. POL-NS-02 reaches the same result (no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the 18:09:40 cancellation), as does POL-NS-06 arithmetically (0 seconds measured against 300 seconds required). The 5.7-minute wait_time_min in the trip record is measured from the false marker and cannot cure the defect.

THE DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS. (1) Compensation under POL-NS-07 is not payable: it is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check was correctly read as not tripping — no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 110, a ratio of about 0.009, so neither the count limb nor the rate limb is met — but that only means nothing withholds a payment that never arises. (2) The fare line is not defective: SGD 4.00 is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) does not disturb the amount. That finding does not make the charge lawful. (3) The escalation argument under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected. There is no unresolved conflict: the apparent tension between the trip record's arrival event and the trace is exactly what POL-NS-05 decides, by deeming the marker false and recomputing the clock, and POL-NS-08(a) finds no clock skew (the 18:04:00 marker coincides with a trace fix, so the skew is well inside 90 seconds). (4) POL-GEN-03's rule that NO_ACTION leaves the charge in place does not apply, because the rider's case displaces the charge.

THE RIDER'S ARGUMENTS. The refund does not depend on rider exoneration. POL-NS-04 is not engaged: limb (a) fails because her only message ('what? no. I'm getting out at the petrol station') refuses an off-platform cash demand rather than locating her, and limb (c) fails because her six fixes sit 319.2 to 321.8 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Her account of being carried in the car is also not supported by the trace she brings (her device reports 0.0 km/h at 320 m from the pin while the vehicle moves at 40 km/h and above). None of that matters here: the refund rests on the driver's own trace, not on the rider's narrative. Her point that the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code cannot bear limb (d) is correct — the code alone does not establish that a required dwell had elapsed, and the platform, not the driver, terminated the trip.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The deciding facts — zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a false arrival marker — are carried by EV-GPS-00625 at weight 1.0, corroborated by EV-TRIP-00625 at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and no deciding fact rests on discounted evidence. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires (confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the conflict is clause-resolved; the counterparty dispute counters are 0 and 0; the anti-farming check does not trip and no_show_disputes_30d is 0; no sole impaired evidence). The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00625-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is cited only for its absence, makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, and decides nothing. The case is therefore decided rather than escalated.

NOTED FOR THE RECORD, NOT REFERRED: the driver's in-app message demanding 'ERP 25 each cash' has no counterpart in the priced ledger (tolls_erp 0.00, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and his own statement concedes he combined two bookings in one vehicle. The only clause-mandated referral this case produces is the false-arrival record under POL-NS-05(ii).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record: record a false-arrival event against driver DRV-32539 on trip TRP-00625 — the 'arrived' marker at 2026-09-25T18:04:00+08:00 places the driver 377.4 m from the pickup pin while travelling above 40 km/h, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.
